'You just want to keep playing': Thorndale's seniors relish chance at an undefeated season
item.description: THORNDALE - In 2023, the Thorndale football team went 0-10 during a season in which they dropped a trio of one-possession games. It was an unusually poor campaign for a program that hadn't had a losing season in six years. But even as the Bulldogs' varsity squad struggled, a talented crop of freshmen was stringing together junior varsity victories. And three years later, that group is now in its final season and has piloted Thorndale to an 8-0 record and a chance at its first district title since 2014. To end that drought, the senior-laden District 13-2A Division I hopefuls will have to beat fellow unbeaten Rosebud-Lott in their final home game of the season Friday night at Bulldog Stadium. "Football is a great sport, but when you go 0-10, you know that year is not as fun," said Cayson Merz, a four-year starter on the offensive line. "When we start playing together, you know, the love for the game just increases tremendously. You just want to keep playing. You don't want it to go away." Thorndale players exit the tunnel ahead of the game against Thrall at Thrall High School on Friday, Aug. 30, 2024 in Thrall, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/American-Statesman) Bouncing back from 0-10 Thorndale's winless ways were short-lived. The Bulldogs went 8-4 in 2024, one year after failing to net a single victory. A number of the current seniors broke through to the varsity ranks that year. Thorndale repeated the record in 2025 with a team led by the current group that's been dominating this year. MORE: Predictions for Austin area's top Week 10 games Although the record was the same, last year offered a glimpse of what has come to fruition this fall. The Bulldogs lost three of their first five games to begin the season before finishing district play on a four-game winning streak. Thorndale also won its bi-district postseason game before falling in the area round to a Ganado team that went 9-1 in the regular season. "Everybody had to kind of up their game a little bit, and we kind of struggled a little bit early with that," Thorndale coach John Kovar said. But his team found its way. "This year they all got to come back in the same roles they played (last year)," the veteran coach added. "Now they're all seniors, a lot of returning starters, a lot of returning experience on both sides of the ball." Thorndale's Hudson Thigpen hugs teammate Kale Meadors as the pair celebrates a big play against Rogers on Sept. 4, 2026. (Markell Irvin/Kellsimage) Strong sendoff season Thorndale has 28 seniors, according to its roster on MaxPreps. And that much time together creates cohesion and trust that aids a team in close games. With this being their farewell campaign, Thorndale's seniors came into the season motivated to leave on a high. item.description: Motorsport photo After the United States Grand Prix, Isack Hadjar was critical of Red Bull's execution, as was Max Verstappen . Both drivers were unhappy with the strategy and, on top of that, were hampered by two problems that have been troubling the Formula 1 team for a long time: technical issues with the team radio and problematic starts. "I have poor radio, I don't even know what's happening. And whenever I drop the clutch, it's going into a nightmare,” Hadjar said in the media pen on Sunday night. “If we fix these two issues, we might already be on the podium. It seems like we can do the hardest things, but we can’t do the silly things.” When asked about those comments during the media day in Mexico, Hadjar acknowledged that he is perfectly entitled to speak his mind about the team – which is, after all, exactly what Red Bull wants: drivers with character and opinions of their own – but that he perhaps could have worded certain things a little differently. “I didn't really think,” he said. “We need to be honest with ourselves as well, but there’s stuff that I should have kept for myself. I know that.” Since then, Red Bull has analysed the race weekend in Texas in detail which revealed that the strategy could indeed have been better, something Hadjar explained further in Mexico. “I think that, as a team, we were probably not open-minded enough to the one-stop strategy,” the Frenchman said when asked about the main lessons from Austin by Motorsport.com. “In a way, we were very convinced that the softer compound was working better. Maybe we thought the degradation was higher than it actually was and once you start with this, we put ourselves in a difficult situation.” Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing That difficult situation led, among other things, to the misunderstanding when Hadjar was supposed to let Verstappen through. The Frenchman did not do so immediately on the long straight towards Turn 12, as the team had asked him to. It briefly caused frustration for Verstappen, but Hadjar clarified that it was not deliberate. It was simply linked to the lack of clarity surrounding the strategy. “I had good pace on the soft, so I didn't want to pit too early. item.title: Anderson 'shocked' by Lancs exit and unsure if he will continue
item.description: James Anderson is England's all-time leading Test wicket-taker with 704 dismissals [Getty Images] England legend James Anderson says he is "sad" and "shocked" by his release by Lancashire and has not decided whether to continue his career at another county. Speaking at length on the Tailenders podcast for the first time since being told he will not have his Lancashire contract renewed, the 44-year-old said the decision made him question whether is "something fundamentally wrong with me as a person". Anderson, England's leading wicket-taker and a Lancashire legend, took 50 wickets in the County Championship and served as captain last season but he was told by Lancashire's new hierarchy they want to build an attack for the future. "I went in for what I thought was a conversation about how the team moves forward," Anderson said. "It wasn't a great year for the team. Being captain I thought it was chat about that. "A couple of minutes in I realised it wasn't a conversation. I was being told they thought the best way for the team to move forward was without me. "I was quite shocked. It was quite brief." Listen to Anderson on latest Tailenders podcast Lancashire's decision was made by their incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace, who held a meeting with Anderson and Lancashire's new chief executive Richard Kenyon. Despite Anderson's wickets, the club finished second bottom in Division Two of the County Championship. In 2024, England also chose to move on from their record wicket-taker in similar circumstances as they attempted to refresh and build an attack for the 2025-26 Ashes in Australia. "All of the way through the season myself and the head coach were like 'is it something we are doing? Could we be doing more to help the team?'" Anderson said. "I finished the season thinking 'was it something I did? Was I doing something wrong?' - and then I get this news. "Now I am thinking that even more. "I am thinking 'this is happening again. Is there something fundamentally wrong with me as a person?' Your head just sort of races. "I wanted to see my career out with Lancs. "I don't know if my career is done, we will have to wait and see, but it would be nice at some point if someone would let me retire." 'I wouldn't have thought so' - Anderson on Yorkshire move The decision has angered Lancashire members and was criticised for being "pretty disrespectful" by Anderson's former England bowling partner Stuart Broad, who said it showed a lack of leadership given the veteran was not given a farewell. Anderson first played List A cricket in 2000 as a 17-year-old for the Lancashire Cricket Board against Suffolk. In addition to his 911 international wickets - an England record and a record for all pace bowlers - Anderson claimed 443 first-class scalps for Lancashire, along with 83 in List A cricket and a further 50 in T20s. item.title: The dashboard misses the mark against Genoa
item.description: GENOA, ITALY - OCTOBER 28: Luciano Spalletti, head coach of Juventus, looks on prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Juventus FC at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on October 28, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) | Getty Images Look, we spend a lot of time in these breakdowns pulling apart positional maps, passing networks, and xG graphics. When a match goes sideways, reaching for the dashboard is almost a natural coping mechanism. It’s our modern safety blanket. It’s what we look at when our stomach is in knots after a miserable 90 minutes. We open up Twitter or fire up our favorite app, hoping to find a chart that proves what we just saw wasn’t as bad as it felt. We search for the structural cog that slipped out of place. We tell ourselves it keeps us honest, stops us from reacting purely on raw emotion, and forces us to focus on process over panic. And if you just look at the numbers from Juventus’ 2–0 loss to Genoa on Wednesday night at the Luigi Ferraris, the stats try their absolute best to sell you a remarkably comfortable story. 63% possession. Over 500 passes completed (at an 87% clip!). 17 total shots fired off. Winning the expected goals battle 1.26 to 1.01. If you were stuck at work and only checked the box score on your phone, you could easily convince yourself of a specific narrative. You could write a clean, tidy statistical post-mortem about Kingsley Ehizibue’s opener taking an unluckily cruel deflection off Andrea Cambiaso. You could talk about how Tommaso Baldanzi caught us out on a rare transition moment for the second. You could shrug it all off as a classic, frustrating case of bad football variance. You could write that article. You could say, “Hey, look at the graphics. We controlled the tempo, we pushed Genoa right back into their own penalty box, and we generated enough volume while conceding very little in terms of raw high-quality chances.” You could write that piece. And for eight out of 10 matches across a long league campaign, that kind of objective, distance-keeping analysis serves us well. But if you actually sat through those 90 minutes on this late-October night in Genoa — if you watched every heavy touch, every slow turn, and every blank stare — you know as well as I do that relying on the dashboard completely misses what was actually happening on that pitch. Before we get into any of the ugly details, we have to be completely fair to where this group is right now. We can’t talk about the loss to Genoa in a vacuum without acknowledging the brutal reality of our injury crisis. When you lose key starting pillars across every single line — sometimes losing multiple options in the exact same position — it creates a heavy, lingering fatigue that runs far deeper than just tired legs. item.title: How social media sleuths used fantasy football clues to leak Chelsea team news
item.description: On arrival at Stamford Bridge last Saturday, a couple of hours before Chelsea’s 5.30pm kick-off against Tottenham, murmurs of a significant injury were already spreading around the press room. Chelsea’s official channels were not revealing any team news, but on social media, the pieces of the puzzle were coming together. At 10am, a fantasy football expert under the name FPL Joe tweeted a graph based on betting markets that showed Chelsea’s projected goals had plummeted from 2.06 the previous day to 1.84 on the morning of the game. Odds markets can be volatile and swings are not always evidence of team changes, but they can hint at something. “Last year we had a couple of instances where we noticed particularly Manchester City, their projected goals were dropping quite sharply before games,” FPL Joe , a software engineer in his day job, tells The Independent . “That, we would infer, turned out to be as a result of Haaland and similar high-impact players having been benched. I could tell that there was data reacting to real things that were happening in the world.” An account called “Team news and ticks” is well known for its reliable leaks, and at 1.45pm it posted: “Some massive assets [players] missing in multiple games today,” in a direct call to the Fantasy Premier League community. Given there were only three more games that day, and Chelsea were the most popular team for fantasy managers, it raised the possibility of an absence among their supreme front three: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro . Joao Pedro did not play a part in the game against Tottenham (PA) Meanwhile, FPL Joe had been digging. A tool called FPL Bot allows anyone to search the 11 million fantasy teams and their managers, which is publicly available information. “It starts with a list,” says Joe. “In my case, it took a bit of time. It’s just doing the research to work out which staff, which players, which family members are most likely candidates for people who might have an FPL account.” At 2.30pm, he posted a diagram analysing the fantasy football teams of several people with links to the Chelsea dressing room, and the changes they had made to their fantasy teams before Friday night’s deadline. It suggested one of Chelsea’s staff had benched Joao Pedro, an odd move with one of the top-scoring fantasy players so far this season. Another X user spotted that a Chelsea employee had apparently transferred the striker out of their team. Another suggested a family member of Morgan Rogers appeared to have sold Joao Pedro and replaced him with Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson – an inspired move before Jackson’s two-goal haul against Manchester City earlier in the day. Joao Pedro was not spotted in pictures of Chelsea players boarding the team bus, and sure enough, the Brazilian was missing from Xabi Alonso ’s squad when the teams were officially announced at 4.15pm. item.title: ‘I could never be that soft’: Michelle Beadle rips Pat McAfee over Utah situation
item.description: Oct 23, 2026; Salt Lake City, Utah, USA; Utah Jazz owner Ryan Smith and ESPN personality Pat McAfee watch play against the New Orleans Pelicans during the first half at Delta Center. Mandatory Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Pat McAfee’s complaints about feeling unsafe at the University of Utah have drawn criticism from all over the sports media world. Now, a former ESPN host is weighing in, and she didn’t hold back. Michelle Beadle argued that women in sports media deal with far worse on a regular basis and would never get away with reacting the way McAfee did. Beadle called it one of the “softest” reactions she has ever seen, adding that she’s enjoying watching the whole thing play out. McAfee vs. Utah College GameDay visited Salt Lake City last weekend for Utah’s matchup with Houston. Before the show, the university shared a video of students doing impressions of McAfee, with one calling him “corny” and another calling him “creepy.” McAfee fired back on the broadcast , picking Houston and telling the Utah crowd that he hoped he’d never see them again. On his show Monday, McAfee said the video made him uncomfortable as he prepared to walk in front of thousands of students, and he referenced the assassination of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University last year. Utah later deleted the video and apologized, while ESPN said it supported McAfee and his concerns about safety. It was also reported this week that the FBI advised McAfee to wear a bulletproof vest for GameDay ‘s first show after Kirk’s death. Still, plenty of critics have accused McAfee of being thin-skinned over what was a lighthearted video. ‘I Could Never Be That Soft’ Beadle, who joined The Dan Le Batard Show on Thursday, pointed out that women in sports media are held to a very different standard. “We are constantly told as women that we’re hysterical, we’re too emotional, we can’t handle things. I can’t tell you how many death and rape threats I’ve gotten via social media since 2009 when we got on Twitter originally. I could never be that soft. Never,” Beadle said on The Dan Le Batard Show . She then took a shot at McAfee’s status in the industry. “This has been one of the softest, and we’ve seen quite a few from some of the people at the top of this food pyramid of sports media, one of the softest reactions to something that was so ridiculously unserious,” Beadle said. Beadle also suggested that McAfee could use a lesson in humility, though she doesn’t expect him to learn one. “I’d like to think people are watching themselves and maybe learning a couple of things. Let it humble you the proper way, but I don’t think that’s what we’re going to see,” she said. “So, quite frankly, from afar, I’m enjoying every single second of it.” The post ‘I could never be that soft’: Michelle Beadle rips Pat McAfee over Utah situation appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Why Kimi Antonelli will be F1’s most surprising champion in 17 years
item.description: Rewinding the clock can prove to be a humbling experience. The ambiguity and anticipation of pre-season guessing games – the inevitable pattern of predictions leading up to day one – can either prove to be a massive feather in the cap come the end of the season (cc. 2025 title prediction ) or an article/video to write off. Yet as this year’s Formula 1 season draws to a close, it is most certainly the latter. All seven of Sky Sports’ experts ? Wrong. BBC pundits ? Wrong. Yours truly ? Wrong. And not just wrong: barely a soul mentioned Kimi Antonelli above George Russell in the 2026 F1 championship stakes. Some bookies, in and around February testing, had the Italian as low as seventh-favourite. George Russell was the heavy favourite for the title in (PA Wire) Fast-forward eight months and Antonelli has a 123-point lead with 125 left on the table. Barring an extremely unlikely scenario – the 20-year-old finishing ninth or lower and Russell or Lewis Hamilton winning the race – Antonelli will be world champion this Sunday under the bright blue skies of Mexico City . If it doesn’t happen this weekend, it’ll happen next week in São Paulo. In essence, barring a season-ending injury, the crowning of Formula 1’s youngest-ever world champion is simply a foregone conclusion. Ironically, Antonelli actually missed media duties on Thursday due to a viral illness, though Mercedes expect him to be fit and ready for practice on Friday. And while it has seemed inevitable for some time, particularly after his wondrous back-to-front triumph at his home grand prix in Monza last month, it is worth recalling just how unfathomable Antonelli’s title triumph had seemed; both at the start of the year and within the wider schism of the sport in the last two decades. Because while he is totally bereft of confidence right now, Russell was anything but at the season-opener in Australia . When it became apparent that Mercedes, as fancied, had the most complete car in this new era of regulations, Russell stormed to pole position and victory at Albert Park. Antonelli, meanwhile, crashed in practice but recovered to finish second on raceday. Russell’s 2025 season, too, only accentuated the likelihood of an inaugural world championship. While witnessing friend, rival and compatriot Lando Norris clinch the title in the quickest car, Russell won two grands prix in sub-standard machinery and finished fourth, best of the rest outside the title contenders. Antonelli, meanwhile, endured a sorry European summer – one full of crashes, mistakes and high emotions – and finished the year in seventh, 159 points behind his teammate. So what we’re talking about now, with five rounds remaining this season, is an incomprehensible points swing. Antonelli’s sheer speed (which we always knew) has been coupled with a composure and maturity beyond his 20 years. He has won nine grands prix while Russell has won just three. item.title: On this day in 1993 – Frank Connor leads Celtic to an unlikely win at Ibrox
item.description: On this day in 1993 – Frank Connor leads Celtic to an unlikely win at Ibrox On this day 33 years ago Celtic headed to Ibrox and were seen by most as the proverbial lambs to the slaughter, but pulled off a major shock to give the large travelling support in the free Broomloan a day to remember in an era of great uncertainty… Celtic’s John Collins and Paul Byrne celebrate Collins’ goal during a Rangers v Celtic match at Ibrox on 30 October 1993. Final score 1-2 to Celtic. Photo The Celtic Wiki Going into the game the Hoops had only managed to win one solitary domestic game in the month of October, and that was a slender 2-1 home win over Dundee. The side however were unbeaten during the guidance of caretaker manager Frank Connor who had taken the reins after the resignation of Liam Brady just three weeks earlier, those being the aforementioned win against Dundee, an away draw at Hibs, and an impressive home win over Sporting Lisbon in the UEFA cup second round first leg. Brian O’Neil scores the late winner for Celtic at Ibrox on 30 October 1993. Photo The Celtic Wiki Connor had made way for new permanent manager Lou Macari who’s first task as Celtic manager was to lead the side into battle in the cauldron of Ibrox, but he allowed the stepping aside Connor to pick and prepare the side for the Derby showdown. Despite a decent display by the Hoops, it was the Ibrox side who opened the scoring in the 67th minute thanks to an Ally McCoist goal, with what many believed to be the winning goal. Celtic had other ideas though, and just three minutes later Ibrox goalkeeper Ally Maxwell blundered by failing to keep hold of a routine ball and John Collins made no mistake as he stroked the ball into the back of the net to level the game much to the delight of the packed Broomloan Road stand. Frank Connor celebrates Celtic’s win at Ibrox on 30 October 1993. Photo The Celtic Wiki Collins goal had looked likely to earn the hoops a hard earned and well deserved point, however deep into injury time that man Collins swung in a terrific corner and Maxwell in the Rangers goal yet again looked unconvincing as Hoops substitute Brian O’Neil who had only entered proceedings as an 88th minute substitute for Charlie Nicholas, headed home from close range to send the Celtic supporters in the Broomloan stand just directly behind the goals into a state of euphoria. Celtic come from behind to beat Rangers at Ibrox on 30 October 1993. The final whistle sounded seconds later, allowing the Celtic players and supporters to celebrate a Derby victory behind enemy lines, one that even the most optimistic of Celtic fans would never ever have visualised. What a delightful, if unexpected, Celtic victory at Ibrox. Incoming Celtic manager Lou Macari in the dugout with caretaker boss Frank Connor at Ibrox as Celtic beat Rangers 2-1 on 30 October 1993. item.title: Kulusevski says 'nervous system changes' behind Spurs return
item.description: Tottenham midfielder Dejan Kulusevski was out of action for 17 months (Glyn KIRK) Dejan Kulusevski has revealed how a "change to my nervous system" enabled him to return with Tottenham after a 17-month injury layoff left him fearing the end of his football career. The Swedish midfielder was introduced to a rapturous reception in the 87th minute of the club's 3-1 home victory against Coventry last week and followed that up with another substitute appearance in Saturday's win at Chelsea as Spurs continued their improvement after a poor start to the Premier League season. Kulusevski had multiple setbacks after knee surgery in May 2025. But a second procedure in March finally set him on the road to recovery. Speaking ahead of Saturday's match against Crystal Palace, the 26-year-old Kulusveski told SpursPlay: "It had been like one year and a couple of months and I still can’t walk on the stairs. I can't walk on the stairs like a normal guy. I have to play football so in my head I'm not going to give up, but I have to think that if this doesn't work out, what do I do? "I went to a physio in Sweden. He was able to change my nervous system and then it felt different. When I did the exercises, I said, 'I don't have pain, like this hurt yesterday. Why is this not hurting today?' "Then I did the next exercise and said, 'this is not hurting,’ and I went into the room to my wife. And I told her, 'it's over, we're going to do this'. From the minute I went into the room, it was better." He added: "There was still pain but it was different. Now I had control of my leg and then that is when the grind started that summer. I started to play football and it got better every day. I was limping and everything, but it was different now. "I got much stronger in a short time and I went from 'this guy will not play football any more’ to playing really good football in just a couple of weeks." The former Juventus winger also paid tribute to Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, saying: "I know from before because he is a very special manager so when he came here, it feels also like it is special." jdg/gj

item.title: Ronaldo closes in on 1,000th goal with hat-trick
item.description: Al-Nassr are second in the Saudi Pro League table [Getty Images] Cristiano Ronaldo's hat-trick helped Al-Nassr to a 5-3 win against Al-Kholood in the Saudi Pro League and took the Portugal striker to 985 career goals. With the game evenly poised at 2-2 following goals from Angelo Gabriel and Sadio Mane for for Al-Nassr, Ronaldo secured the win for his side by scoring three times in 15 second-half minutes. His Portugal team-mate Joao Felix contributed four assists, including for two of Ronaldo's goals. It was the 67th hat-trick of the 41-year-old's career as he continues to chase another milestone in a glittering career. He has scored seven of his hat-tricks for Al-Nassr - along with 44 for Real Madrid, 10 for Portugal and three each at Manchester United and Juventus. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia and is the all-time top goalscorer in men's international football. He has spent almost four years at Saudi Pro League champions Al-Nassr, with whom he has one year remaining on his contract. In August, he hinted at retirement by saying it was "probably" his last year playing. Al-Nassr are defending champions in the Saudi Pro League and sit second in the table, although they have a game in hand on leaders Al-Qadsiah. item.title: Vuelve el nerviosismo en el Barça: Raphinha convocado con Brasil
item.description: Vuelve el nerviosismo en el Barça: Raphinha convocado con Brasil El futbolista brasileño ha sido convocado por Ancelotti para disputar los amistosos contra Japón y Singapur el próximo noviembre A partir del próximo 9 de noviembre hay un nuevo parón de selecciones: dos semanas que ponen en vilo a todos los clubes que tienen algún internacional, a la espera de que ninguno regrese lesionado. Eso es lo que le pasa al FC Barcelona con Raphinha . El jugador brasileño ha vuelto a ser convocado por el seleccionador de la ‘canarinha’ para disputar dos partidos amistosos contra Japón (14 de noviembre) y Singapur (17 de noviembre) . La disputa de esos partidos supondrá, nuevamente, una importante suma de kilómetros para la estrella azulgrana. Raphinha recorrerá unos 22.000 kilómetros . Raphinha en el duelo ante el PSG. | Europa Press Cabe recordar que el futbolista volvió lesionado del último parón y se perdió los partidos contra Getafe y Galatasaray . Como es lógico después de una lesión, el jugador debe coger ritmo de competición. Desde su vuelta al césped, Raphinha no ha disputado ningún partido completo. Suma 20′ contra el Betis, 60′ contra el PSG y 86′ ante el Real Madrid. Es decir, de 270 minutos posibles , Raphinha ha disputado 166′ , lo que hace un 61,4% de los minutos . Tampoco ha vuelto a su mejor nivel: no está tan eléctrico como antes y sus cotas goleadoras han disminuido sensiblemente, con solo un gol desde su regreso . Aun sin estar al 100% de forma física, Carlo Ancelotti ha decidido convocarlo para dos amistosos intrascendentes . El historial reciente del atacante blaugrana no invita al optimismo en Can Barça. Contando el último parón, Raphinha ha vuelto lesionado a Barcelona de las últimas tres llamadas de la selección . La primera por disputar un amistoso contra Francia en Estados Unidos, que le supuso perderse los dos meses más importantes de la pasada campaña . La segunda, tras el Mundial, y la reciente tras disputar dos amistosos irrelevantes en India y Australia . Ancelotti responde a Laporta y defiende la convocatoria de Raphinha Después de la lesión del gaúcho en el último parón de selecciones, Laporta se mostró indignado, declarando que los clubes sufren «grandes perjuicios» . Sin embargo, Ancelotti ha vuelto a convocar a Raphinha y ha contestado al presidente azulgrana. No tenemos peticiones particulares, tampoco las necesitamos. En las fechas FIFA llamaremos a los futbolistas que consideremos relevantes para la selección brasileña. Asimismo, el técnico italiano ha defendido la convocatoria del internacional brasileño. Hemos escogido cinco futbolistas que estuvieron en el último Mundial y que serán importantes para este nuevo ciclo en el que disputaremos la Copa América y una nueva Copa del Mundo. Estos jugadores son Marquinhos, Gabriel Magalhães, Bruno Guimarães, Vinícius Júnior y Raphinha. - Publicidad -

item.title: Arsenal appeal rejected despite ex-ref arguing against red card
item.description: Arsenal appeal rejected despite ex-ref arguing against red card The FA have confirmed that they won’t be overturning Max Dowman’s red card, despite former referees arguing that it was a wrongful dismissal. Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images Arsenal youngster Max Dowman was sent off in the latter stages of the Gunners’ League Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town in midweek, briefly reducing the team to 10 men. But the bigger impact is that Dowman is now out of action for three domestic fixtures, missing the matches against Liverpool , Hull City , and Newcastle United . The only positive is that he’ll be available for the Champions League match against Slavia Praha in between. Given the injury to Bukayo Saka and doubts around the fitness of Noni Madueke , as well as the fact that Christos Tzolis has been out of action for a couple of weeks, Arsenal could obviously do without losing Dowman. But their attempt to appeal the red card has already been rejected. Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images The FA published a statement on Thursday, saying: “An independent Regulatory Commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Max Dowman. “The Arsenal player was sent off during their EFL Cup game against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday 27 October and will be suspeneded for three matches. “The Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decisions will be published in due course.” Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images The decision comes in spite of the fact that former Premier League referees like Mark Halsey had spoken out against the red card. Dowman was on the end of a heavy challenge, and he reacted with a swing of his leg. But subsequent replays have shown that Dowman was trying to throw off the opponent’s leg, not to kick it, and Halsey didn’t think it met the threshold for violent conduct. “It’s petulance, it’s not violent, it’s not violent conduct,” Halsey said . “He’s adopted an aggressive attitude towards an opponent, and you can understand why. “Obviously, difficult for referee Michael Salisbury in real time…I thought it was unfortunate [on Tuesday night] to receive a red card for violent conduct. While the win over the Hoosiers was massive, the Buckeyes paid a steep price in Bloomington, losing quarterback Julian Sayin to injury. Where Ohio State stands The victory over Indiana was Ohio State’s 30th win on the road since 2019, which is tied with Boise State for most in the country during that span.
